title: Relations and Functions: Chapter Introduction
subject: Mathematics
objective: Roll numbers and birthdays are both functions, but only roll numbers are one-one. The chapter classifies relations and functions and shows which functions can be reversed.

fill.q: A function gives every input exactly ____ output.
A function in which different inputs always give different outputs is called ____.
A function in which every element of the co-domain is an image is called ____.
A function that is both one-one and onto is called ____.
A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive is an ____ relation.

tf.explain: Each student has exactly one birthday.
Two students can share a birthday, so it is many-one.

tf.q: "Is in the same class as" is an equivalence relation.
tf.explain: It is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

ar.a: f(x) = x² on ℝ has no inverse.
ar.r: f is not one-one on ℝ.
ar.explain: A function needs to be bijective to be invertible.

ar.a: Roll-number assignment for 40 students using 1-40 is invertible.

options: student → phone numbers of all friends
mcq.explain: One student can have many friends' numbers.

mcq.q: f: ℝ → ℝ, f(x) = x² is:

mcq.explain: Distinct x give distinct values and every real number is reached.

mcq.q: The relation "is the father of" on people is:
mcq.explain: No one is their own father; it is not symmetric or transitive.

num.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = 2x + 3 on ℝ.

num.answer: Yes, it is an equivalence relation

short.q: Distinguish a relation from a function with an example.
short.solution: A relation is any set of pairs linking A to B; a function is a relation in which every element of A has exactly one image. Student → friends is a relation, student → roll number is a function.

short.q: Why is student → birthday a function but not one-one?
short.solution: Each student has exactly one birthday (function), but two different students can have the same birthday, so different inputs can share an output (many-one).

right: Every element of B is used
